{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-03",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Payment webhook endpoint", "Order service"],
    "dataStores": ["Orders store"],
    "externalServices": ["Payment provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Public internet to webhook endpoint"],
    "dataClasses": ["payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Anyone can forge payment events because the webhook has no sender verification",
      "scenario": "The webhook URL is public and accepts any JSON body, with no signature, shared secret or mutual TLS proving the payment provider sent it. An attacker who guesses or discovers the URL posts {order id, status: paid} and the order is marked paid without any money moving, so goods ship for free. Repeating this for many order ids turns into bulk fraud.",
      "component": "Payment webhook endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "money" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The endpoint is public and accepts any JSON body with an order id and status." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V13.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306", "CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone on the internet can tell your system an order was paid, so they get goods without paying.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify the payment provider signature on every inbound webhook",
        "given": "a public payment webhook endpoint",
        "when": "a request arrives",
        "then": "the server verifies the provider's signature over the raw body using a secret held only by the server, and rejects any request with a missing or invalid signature before any order is touched"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Server trusts the status field in the request body to decide an order is paid",
      "scenario": "The design takes the order id and status from the request body and marks the order paid on that basis alone, instead of fetching the authoritative payment record from the provider or matching the captured amount and currency to the order. An attacker (or a legitimate but altered provider payload) can set status to paid, or downgrade a refunded or failed payment, changing financial state the client should not control.",
      "component": "Order service payment status update",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "money" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Our payment webhook endpoint receives events from the payment provider and marks orders as paid." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.5.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-602", "CWE-20"],
      "plainLanguage": "The system believes whatever the incoming message says about payment instead of checking with the payment provider.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Confirm payment server-side before marking an order paid",
        "given": "a verified webhook event for an order",
        "when": "the handler processes it",
        "then": "the server re-reads the payment from the provider API by payment id and only marks the order paid when the provider reports a successful capture whose amount and currency match the order total"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Replaying a captured webhook call repeatedly re-applies the same payment",
      "scenario": "Any JSON body is accepted with no event id, nonce or timestamp and no record of events already processed. An attacker who captures or crafts one valid-looking call can resend it many times; a repeated paid event can re-trigger fulfilment, loyalty credit or refund flows for the same order, or be reused after an order is cancelled.",
      "component": "Payment webhook endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "money" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The endpoint is public and accepts any JSON body with an order id and status." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V13.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-294"],
      "plainLanguage": "The same payment message can be sent again and again, and the system acts on it each time.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Make webhook processing idempotent and reject stale events",
        "given": "an inbound webhook event",
        "when": "it carries an event id already recorded, or a timestamp outside a short tolerance window",
        "then": "the server returns success without re-applying any state change, and each event id is applied to an order at most once"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Order id in the body lets an attacker act on other customers' orders",
      "scenario": "The handler acts on whatever order id it is handed, with no check that the event belongs to a payment the provider actually created for that order and no owner binding. An attacker iterates or guesses order ids and flips other customers' orders to paid, or marks orders that were never purchased, altering records across the whole order base.",
      "component": "Order lookup by client-supplied order id",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts any JSON body with an order id and status" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "By changing the order number in the message, someone can mess with anyone else's order.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind each event to the payment intent recorded on the order",
        "given": "a verified event naming an order id",
        "when": "the handler loads that order",
        "then": "it proceeds only when the event's payment or session id matches the identifier stored on that order at checkout, and otherwise rejects and alerts"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Unauthenticated webhook can be flooded to stall real payment confirmations",
      "scenario": "Because the endpoint needs no credential, a bot can send a high volume of large or malformed JSON bodies. Each one costs a parse and an order-store write or lookup, so the queue of genuine provider callbacks backs up and real paid orders are never confirmed, which blocks fulfilment and loses revenue rather than just slowing a page.",
      "component": "Payment webhook endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "availability" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The endpoint is public" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can spam the payment webhook until genuine payment confirmations stop getting through.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Cheaply reject unverified webhook traffic before doing work",
        "given": "inbound requests to the webhook",
        "when": "a request fails signature verification, exceeds a maximum body size, or arrives from a source above a per-source rate threshold",
        "then": "it is dropped before any parsing or order-store access, and genuine provider callbacks are processed from a bounded queue"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No way to tell a forged payment confirmation from a genuine one after the fact",
      "scenario": "With no sender authentication and no stored provider event identity, a paid order carries no proof of which event caused it. When fraud is discovered, staff cannot distinguish attacker-injected confirmations from real provider events, so chargebacks and losses cannot be traced or reversed accurately. This matters here specifically because the only trigger for marking money received is an unauthenticated request.",
      "component": "Order payment audit trail",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "receives events from the payment provider and marks orders as paid" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V16.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If fake payment messages get in, there is no record showing which payments were real.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record the verified provider event behind every payment state change",
        "given": "an order whose status changes to paid",
        "when": "the change is written",
        "then": "the stored record includes the provider event id, payment id, amount, currency and signature verification result, in a form that cannot be altered by the request sender"
      }
    }
  ]
}
